solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like the cerebrum, initially large in the brainy, amazingly

indicators.note: initially says to take only the opening letter of the word large
amazingly suggests the letters of in the brainy are thrown into a startling new order

explanation.surface: A description of the brain's folded outer layer, appropriately found inside a clever head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazingly' rearranges IN THE BRAINY into ABYRINTHINE, after L from 'initially large'. The surface's 'brainy' is fodder, not a description.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebrum's surface is deeply folded and convoluted, so it resembles a maze, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Heads of local office to set up and initiate office at station?

indicators.note: heads are the leading letters of the words local and office

parts.note: to stand something, such as a ladder, is to set it up
to found a business is to initiate or establish it

explanation.surface: Instructions to the heads of a local branch on setting up and launching a new office.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' of the answer comes inside STAND, so the clue's 'and' is just a link. The question mark marks the definition as an example: one such office is at a railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway stations traditionally have a lost property office where mislaid items are handed in and reclaimed.

clue.text: Beer half-heartedly produced for nipper

indicators.note: the heart of the beer word is a doubled letter, and half-heartedly keeps only half of that pair

parts.note: bitter is a British style of beer, a hoppy pale ale

explanation.surface: A beer brewed without enthusiasm for a child.
explanation.walkthrough: BITTER is a traditional British draught ale. Its heart is TT; losing one T leaves the answer. 'Nipper' looks like British slang for a child, but here it is something that nips.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that nips, such as a dog or insect, bites, so a nipper is one that bites.

clue.text: Reply regarding limiting one comment on forum

indicators.note: limiting means the regarding word bounds the others, holding them inside

parts.note: re is a short word meaning regarding or concerning
I is the Roman numeral for one
a post is a message left on an internet forum

explanation.surface: Answering about the restriction of a single remark on an online message board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regarding' looks like a link meaning 'concerning the reply', but it supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp retort, a kind of reply made in conversation or fencing.

clue.text: Aristocrat getting a couple of pounds extra

parts.note: a nob is informal British slang for an upper-class person
L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra), so two of them make a pair of Ls

explanation.surface: A nobleman receiving a little extra cash.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an illegal delivery by the bowler is called a no-ball, and it gives the batting side a run counted as an 'extra'.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, runs not scored off the bat are extras, and an illegal delivery is one kind, adding a penalty run.

clue.text: They've come into money? Girl's embracing one

indicators.note: embracing means the possessive word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: hers means belonging to a girl or woman
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl's lucky inheritance, and she has a hug for somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts I inside HERS. The question mark flags a definition that describes the answer loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who inherit an estate receive the money left to them, so they have come into money.

clue.text: Overlook large general being upset: shocking treatment!

indicators.note: being upset in a down clue means the pieces are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
Gen is the abbreviation for the military rank General
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, treatment by electric shock

explanation.surface: A senior officer, disregarded and shocked by his rough handling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being upset' turns L GEN upwards into NEGL.
explanation.definitionFit: To neglect something is to fail to attend to it, which is to overlook it.

clue.text: Claim mastery, after working: that's irregular

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of claim mastery are being worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of skill after a job, but the outcome is uneven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges CLAIM MASTERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking symmetry is uneven or lopsided in shape, so it is irregular.

clue.text: Prepare dominant position in tennis

definitions.meaning: to prepare something is to arrange or establish it ready for use
being a set ahead in a tennis match is a commanding lead

explanation.surface: Getting ready to take the upper hand in a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something up is to prepare it, and a player one set ahead is said to be a set up.

clue.text: New union members accepting good connections

indicators.note: accepting means the marriage word takes the other letter into itself

parts.note: brides are newly joined partners in a marriage union

explanation.surface: Fresh trade union recruits welcoming useful contacts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union, but it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridges span gaps and link two places, and figuratively they are links between people or ideas.

clue.text: Look pained, turning round after a spray

indicators.note: after places the reversed pieces following the letter A
turning round means the two words are read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold
sore means hurting or pained

explanation.surface: Someone grimaces in pain, turning away after an attack of spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning round' gives EROSOL. 'Look pained' reads as one phrase about a facial expression, but splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised can that releases its contents as a fine mist, so it is a spray.

clue.text: Power in second eleven, perhaps

parts.note: a cricket or football eleven is an example of a team

explanation.surface: Strength among a club's reserve players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second eleven' reads as a reserve side; split, it is S and an example of a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam drove engines in the industrial age, so it serves as a source of power.

clue.text: Mother's left to adopt English girl

indicators.note: to adopt means the outer pieces take the other letter in, as a family takes in a child

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, so dam's means the mother's

explanation.surface: A mother departs in order to take in an English girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to adopt' puts E inside DAMS + L.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an old-fashioned or literary word for a young woman or maiden.

clue.text: French detective, one appearing in magazine about origin of thefts

indicators.note: appearing in means the numeral sits inside the magazine word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
re means about or concerning

indicators.note: origin of says to take the opening letter of thefts

explanation.surface: A French sleuth featured in a magazine story about a spate of thefts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' puts the numeral inside the magazine word; Maigret is Georges Simenon's Paris policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Jules Maigret is the Paris police detective in Georges Simenon's crime novels.

clue.text: Minor untruth about odd items in total

indicators.note: about means the untruth wraps round the picked letters

parts.note: a lie is an untruth

indicators.note: odd items are the first, third and fifth letters of the word total

explanation.surface: A small fib concerning odd things in the overall sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd items in' means the odd-numbered letters of 'total', not strange objects; 'about' wraps the fib round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minor is small or unimportant, which is the sense of little here.

clue.text: Fish is given to friend in a perfect world

parts.note: the ide is a European freshwater fish, a crossword favourite
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A fish handed to a companion makes for a perfect world.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means under the best possible circumstances, as things would be if all went to plan.

clue.text: French race venue tends to receive millions

indicators.note: to receive means the tends word takes the other letter inside

parts.note: to lean towards something is to tend to it
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A French motor-racing town tends to take in millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to receive' puts M inside LEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: The French town hosts the famous 24-hour motor race, so it is a venue for racing.

clue.text: Tree not recorded after start of operation

indicators.note: after places the broadcast word following that letter
start of says to take the opening letter of operation

parts.note: a live broadcast is transmitted as it happens, not recorded

explanation.surface: A tree, unrecorded after the beginning of a surgical procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is a Mediterranean evergreen grown for its fruit and oil.

clue.text: Nice description of repealed legislation?

parts.note: ex means former, as a repealed law no longer stands
an act is a law passed by parliament

explanation.surface: A neat way to describe a law that has been scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' at the start looks like the French city or 'pleasant'; it means precise. The whole clue also reads as a cryptic hint, a former law.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its older sense means fine or precise, as in a nice distinction, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Voter part reversed about spinning etc.

indicators.note: about means the turned-round word goes round the other letters
reversed means the word for part is read backwards

parts.note: a role is an actor's part

indicators.note: spinning suggests the letters of etc are twirled into a new order

explanation.surface: A voter's role turned around concerning spin and so forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' gives ELOR and 'spinning' gives ECT; 'about' wraps ELOR round ECT.
explanation.definitionFit: An elector is a person entitled to vote in an election.

clue.text: Thrill — not half — over start of bass beat

indicators.note: not says the named part of the word thrill is left out of it

parts.note: half here is the back half of the word thrill, its last three letters
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over, a set of six balls

indicators.note: start of says to take the opening letter of the word bass

explanation.surface: A musician feels a thrill, but not half as much, at the opening of a bass beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' drops ILL, the back half of Thrill, leaving THR. O is cricket's abbreviation for an over. 'Bass beat' reads as music, but 'beat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular pulse, such as a heartbeat, so it is a beat.

clue.text: Vehicle in rain misrepresented as a blissful state

indicators.note: in means the vehicle word sits inside the other letters
misrepresented suggests the letters of rain are shown in a false order

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Driving a van in the rain wrongly passed off as heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' gives NIRA; 'in' puts the vehicle inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism, nirvana is the ultimate state of release from suffering, so it means perfect bliss.

clue.text: Some remarkably rich words for a song

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some unusually rich words written for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is the text of a song, the words sung to the tune.

clue.text: Evidence of worth, as most subtly altered

indicators.note: altered says the letters of as most subtly are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Proof of value, as most people would subtly change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges AS MOST SUBTLY; 'subtly' looks like it modifies the indicator but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A possession such as a luxury car is flaunted to show wealth or rank, so it is evidence of worth.
